Manufacturing NDT training in Wichita: the short answer

Manufacturing NDT training in Wichita prepares technicians to inspect welds, castings, forgings, machined parts and assemblies in the city's fabrication shops, HVAC and equipment plants, and the supplier base around its aircraft factories. Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in MT, PT, UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, VT and ET, live online or onsite at your Wichita facility, led by an ASNT Level III. Quotes are on request.

Wichita is a manufacturing town that happens to be famous for aircraft. Behind the airframe plants sits a wide supplier base of machine shops, sheet-metal and structural fabricators, heat treaters, finishing and plating shops, and equipment builders for agriculture, energy and HVAC. Most of those shops are not aerospace primes, most of them certify (if they certify at all) under SNT-TC-1A, and most of them need a small number of well-trained Level IIs and access to a Level III rather than a full in-house school. That is the gap this page is about.

Request a Wichita manufacturing NDT training quote, or read on for methods, schemes and options.

Manufacturing NDT work in Wichita

Wichita's employer base is the backdrop for every NDT hire in the city. Public employer lists from the Greater Wichita Partnership and the city put aircraft builders at the top: the aerostructures plant that Boeing took back when it completed its acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems, Textron Aviation, and Bombardier's Wichita site. Johnson Controls runs a large HVAC equipment plant. Around them are hundreds of suppliers. We name these only as context for where the work is; Atlantis has no relationship with them.

For a manufacturing NDT technician, that translates into several distinct kinds of work:

  • Weld fabrication. Structural steel, frames for agricultural and industrial equipment, skids, tanks and pressure parts. VT is the first gate, MT the usual surface method on carbon steel, and UT or RT where full-penetration welds need volumetric acceptance.
  • Machined parts and forgings. Suppliers machining steel, aluminium and titanium parts check for surface cracks with PT and MT and for internal flaws in forgings and bar with UT.
  • Castings. RT for internal soundness against reference radiographs, PT and MT for surfaces, and UT for wall thickness.
  • HVAC and equipment manufacturing. Brazed and welded joints, coil and frame fabrication, and supplier part inspection. Much of this is production-line VT and PT, with leak testing handled as its own discipline.
  • Aerospace supply chain. Parts heading to the airframe plants are inspected to the customer's specification and, often, by NAS 410 certified personnel. That is where the two certification worlds meet in Wichita; see the scheme table below.
  • Oil and gas equipment. Kansas has long-running oil production, and Wichita shops build and repair tanks, separators, pipe spools and pump components for it. That work runs to ASME, API and customer specs.

The industrial side of the city is covered in our general NDT training in Wichita page, and the aircraft side in aerospace NDT training in Wichita. This page stays with the manufacturing and fabrication shops.

Methods used in Wichita manufacturing, and the codes behind them

MethodManufacturing application in WichitaCode / standard (context)
VTWeld visual acceptance before any other method, fit-up and dimensional checks, production-line visual on brazed jointsAWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 (bridges), ASME VIII, customer specs
MTSurface and near-surface cracks on carbon-steel welds, forgings, shafts and equipment framesASTM E709, ASTM E1444, AWS D1.1
PTNon-magnetic parts: aluminium, stainless and titanium machined parts, castings, brazed jointsASTM E165, ASTM E1417 (aerospace suppliers)
UTFull-penetration weld acceptance, forging and bar inspection, thickness checksAWS D1.1 Clause 8, ASME V Article 4/5, ASTM A388
PAUTFaster weld inspection with an imaging record, replacing RT on some pressure and structural workASME V Article 4, AWS D1.1 (where qualified), customer approval
TOFDThick-section pressure vessel welds, usually paired with PAUTASME V Article 4, ASME code cases
RTCastings against reference radiographs, pressure-part and pipe-spool weldsASME V Article 2, ASTM E446/E186 reference radiographs, Kansas radiation rules
ETConductivity and heat-treat verification on aluminium, tube and bar inspection, surface cracks on machined partsASTM E1004, ASTM E426, customer specs

If you are a welder or fabricator moving into inspection, MT and UT usually come first. See the MT Level II course and the UT Level II course. Machine and casting shops more often start with the PT Level II course or the RT Level II course.

A method spotlight for Wichita: MT and UT on fabricated steel

Fabrication shops in Wichita produce a lot of welded carbon steel, and most of their NDT scope is MT and UT. A good MT technician understands field direction, yoke versus prod technique, wet versus dry particles, lighting and demagnetisation, and how AWS D1.1 acceptance criteria are written. A good UT technician can calibrate on the right block, scan a full-penetration weld with the correct angle and coverage, size indications and write a report the customer accepts. Both are teachable in a structured way, and both fail in the same place: technicians who learned on the job without the theory. Our onsite courses use your own welds and blocks for practice so the training transfers directly to your production work.

Which certification scheme Wichita manufacturers expect

SchemeWho in Wichita typically requires itDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?

See NAS 410 certification requirements

ASME Section V / VIIIPressure-vessel and boiler shops, whose NDT personnel are normally certified under SNT-TC-1AYes, through SNT-TC-1A

The practical consequence: a Wichita fabrication technician certified under SNT-TC-1A can work most of the city's manufacturing scope. Moving into NAS 410 work at an aircraft builder means that employer recertifies you under its own programme, often after additional hours and examinations.

The SNT-TC-1A path for Wichita manufacturing technicians

  1. The employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. Your company writes and owns the written practice. If you do not have one, start with written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Method theory, equipment, technique, codes and acceptance criteria. Required hours depend on method and level, and your written practice may set them higher. See the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged under a certified technician on real production parts.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations. Administered by a Level III, with specific questions on the codes and procedures your shop actually uses.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, annually.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer certifies. Recertification follows your written practice.

More on the employer side: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiation licensing and other Kansas requirements

Kansas is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials used in industrial radiography are licensed by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment through its Radiation Control Program, which also handles X-ray registration. Radiographers working with sources must meet the certification and training requirements that come with those licences. If your shop uses a cabinet X-ray or a digital radiography system, registration and safety rules still apply; check the current requirements with KDHE before you plan RT training. Atlantis teaches radiographic technique and film or digital interpretation under SNT-TC-1A; we do not issue radiation safety credentials.

Shops working on defence-related parts may have access, export-control and citizenship rules from their customers. Those are employer matters, not training matters, but they affect who can be trained on which parts.

How Atlantis delivers manufacturing NDT training in Wichita

We have no training centre in Wichita and no walk-in classroom anywhere. Instead:

  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led course at your Wichita plant, on your equipment, using your welds, castings and calibration blocks. For a production shop this is usually the most efficient model: no travel, and the practical work is on your parts.
  • Live online. Real-time instructor-led classroom sessions for individuals or small groups. See online NDT training.
  • Blended. Theory online across a few weeks, then an onsite block for practicals and examinations.

We plan sessions around production. A cohort can be split across shifts, and training can be timed around a plant's slow periods or customer audits. Ask about onsite training for your Wichita crew. Onsite and cohort quotes come back within one business day. For the cohort model in more detail, see corporate NDT training.

Level III services and written practices for Wichita shops

Many Wichita suppliers need an outside Level III: to write or update a written practice, to prepare and administer examinations, to review procedures and technique sheets, or to get ready for a customer audit. Atlantis provides that under SNT-TC-1A. If a customer starts flowing down NAS 410 requirements, we can explain what changes, while being clear that a NAS 410 Responsible Level 3 must be appointed under that standard. For local consulting see steel NDT consulting in Wichita and aerospace NDT consulting in Wichita, or book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments, including a welding workshop and an NDT lab, which match most Wichita manufacturing scope. Trainees can practise probe handling, scan coverage and indication recognition between sessions. It is practice only and does not replace the practical examination on real specimens. Wichita users can also start at Practical NDT for Wichita.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and written-practice work.

Moving from welding into NDT in Wichita

Wichita has a large welding and fabrication workforce, and welders make strong NDT technicians because they already understand joint design and how defects form. The usual step is VT and MT first, then UT. Our article on the welder to NDT technician path walks through it. On funding: GI Bill and WIOA money generally goes to approved schools and programmes. Atlantis does not claim that approval, so our training is usually employer-sponsored; KANSASWORKS can tell you which programmes are currently approved.

Frequently asked questions about manufacturing NDT training in Wichita

Where can I get manufacturing NDT training in Wichita?

WSU Tech runs a college NDT programme, local providers offer short courses, large employers train in-house, and Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A training live online or onsite at your Wichita facility.

Which NDT method should a Wichita fabrication shop train first?

Usually VT and MT for carbon-steel welding, then UT for full-penetration weld acceptance. Machine and casting shops more often start with PT and RT.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted by Wichita aerospace suppliers?

For many non-aerospace customers, yes. Parts going to aircraft builders often need NAS 410 certified personnel, which the employer certifies under its own programme. Check your purchase orders for flow-down requirements.

How long does MT or UT Level II training take?

Under SNT-TC-1A, it depends on the method, level and your written practice: classroom hours plus on-the-job experience. See the training requirements matrix.

Can I take NDT training online in Kansas?

Yes, the classroom portion can be taken live online. Practical examinations must be done on real specimens, typically at your employer's facility.

Do I need a license for radiography in Kansas?

Radioactive sources and X-ray equipment are regulated by KDHE's Radiation Control Program, and radiographers must meet the certification and training requirements tied to those licences. NDT training on its own does not license you.

What does NDT training cost in Wichita?

We quote on request. Cost depends on methods, levels, number of trainees, online versus onsite delivery, and whether examinations and written-practice work are included. Onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Can you train our whole shift at our Wichita plant?

Yes. We run onsite cohorts and can split sessions across shifts. Ask for a Wichita cohort quote.

Do you offer CWI or NAS 410 training?

No. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. We mention CWI and NAS 410 because Wichita employers ask for them alongside NDT certification.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training in Wichita?

Generally only at approved schools and programmes, which Atlantis does not claim to be. Ask your employer about sponsorship, or check KANSASWORKS and the VA for approved options.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Wichita employers?

SNT-TC-1A certification is widely used by Wichita's fabrication, equipment and energy manufacturers. Remember that it is employer-based and generally does not transfer automatically between employers.

What do NDT technicians earn in Wichita?

We do not publish city salary figures. See our NDT salary guide for published ranges and sources.
